source: A wheel and axle turn together: a small turn of the axle makes a big turn of the wheel, or the other way. A pulley is a wheel with a rope; a movable pulley halves the pull you need.
Thinking a single fixed pulley at the top makes lifting lighter. It only changes the direction: you pull down to lift up. A movable pulley, or more pulleys, makes the pull smaller.
A doorknob, a steering wheel and a screwdriver handle all look different, but they work the same way: a big wheel turns a small axle.

In a wheel and axle, a big wheel and a small rod (the axle) turn together. Turning the big wheel takes less force to turn the axle. A pulley is a wheel with a rope in its groove. A fixed pulley changes the direction of your pull. A movable pulley halves the pull you need.
A wheel and axle, and a pulley.
(Real pulleys have a little friction, so you pull a bit more than this.)
Why does a flagpole have a pulley at the top?
It changes the direction of the pull.
You cannot climb up to lift the flag.
The fixed pulley lets you pull the rope down at the bottom to raise the flag up.
Thinking a single fixed pulley makes things lighter. It only lets you pull in an easier direction.
